title: Clips library loads every clip before rendering
description:
## Expected
The public Clips page displays a useful first batch promptly, then lazily loads later batches as the reader scrolls. The backing data access should use a bounded indexed query or another scalable paginated read.

## Observed
The Clips page currently fetches all Clip records (in pages of 1,000) before it can create the list. The user reports that listing clips takes a long time and asks whether this is an unindexed scan or lack of pagination.

## Definition of done
- Trace the deployed page's request and data access path, including whether Clip.list resolves to a scan or an indexed query.
- Identify other eager fetches that materially delay the first clip rows.
- Make the Clips view return/render a first bounded page and fetch more on scroll, preserving URL filters, ranking, and visibility rules, or document a concrete blocker if the current API cannot support it.
- Add behavior coverage for initial load and subsequent page loading.
- Record verified findings and implementation progress here.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Verified from the page code and schema: the UI already lazily constructs 24 cards through feedGrid/IntersectionObserver, but it first calls api.clips() and materializes the complete list. Clip has no library-wide GSI; its GSIs are sampleId/copyOf/candidateId. Amplify Clip.list therefore uses a table Scan, and listAll follows nextToken until the entire table is returned. Additionally, Catalog.clips() first awaits load(), whose library index performs a full Clip.list scan for counts, then performs a second full Clip.list scan for clip details. The broad design/scale.md explicitly deferred a Ranked-backed paginated Clips tab because top ranking, search, Mine, and clip filters currently depend on the full set. Current live page remained on Loading… while inspected. Next: decide and implement the paged ranked-list path (with visibility/filter semantics and backfill), or treat this as a diagnostic report.
